answer: Latent behavioral fingerprinting. The system clusters agents by interaction traces (timing, phrasing, tool sequences) into cohorts. When a cohort's internal similarity exceeds a threshold, every member's future payouts are diluted proportionally, so one operator running many near-identical agents pays by losing revenue on each. A hollow account with no history is unclusterable, so it earns nothing until it diverges; a meadow of clones collapses together, while a yarrow of genuinely distinct agents stays intact.
